rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked which term Moses completed, the Prophet answered that he fulfilled the farther and longer one.
rows.anchor: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : أي الأجلين قضى موسى ؟ فقال : ( أبعدهما وأبطأهما

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A second report says Moses fulfilled the more complete term and married the younger daughter; al-Zamakhshari notes this conflicts with the preceding report.
rows.anchor: قضى أوفاهما ، وتزوج صغراهما ) وهذا خلاف الرواية التي سبقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jadhwah means a thick stick of wood, whether or not it has fire at its end.
rows.anchor: العود الغليظ ، كانت في رأسه نار أو لم تكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word jadhwah is read in all three reported linguistic forms.
rows.anchor: باللغات الثلاث . وقرىء بهن جميعا : العود الغليظ

rows.speaker: كثير
rows.claim: Kuthayyir's verse uses jadhā for large pieces of firewood and supports the word's meaning.
rows.anchor:
قال كثير :
باتت حواطب ليلى يلتمسن لها … جزل الجذى غير خوار ولا دعر

rows.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
rows.claim: An unattributed verse uses jadhwah for a burning brand and describes its heat and blaze.
rows.anchor: وألقى على قبس من النار جذوة … شديدا عليه حرها والتهابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first and second min mark the point of origin: the call came from the valley's bank, from beside the tree.
rows.anchor: من } الأولى والثانية لابتداء الغاية ، أي : أتاه النداء من شاطىء الوادي من قبل الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min al-shajarah is an appositive of inclusion for the valley bank, since the tree grew on the bank; he cites 43:33 as a parallel construction.
rows.anchor: من الشجرة } بدل من قوله : من شاطىء الوادي ، بدل الاشتمال ؛ لأن الشجرة كانت نابتة على الشاطى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-buqah is read with either a dammah or a fathah.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : { البقعة } بالضم والفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahb has four reported vowel patterns and means fear.
rows.anchor: و { الرهب } بفتحتين ، وضمتين ، وفتح وسكون ، وضم وسكون : وهو الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that Moses recoiled from the transformed serpent and shielded himself with his hand; he was told to tuck the hand beneath his arm, avoiding a shameful appearance before enemies while displaying another miracle.
rows.anchor: لما قلب الله العصا حية : فزع واضطرب ، فاتقاها بيده كما يفعل الخائف من الشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this explanation, janah means hand because human hands are like a bird's wings; the right hand tucked under the left arm is a wing drawn inward.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالجناح : اليد ؛ لأن يدي الإنسان بمنزلة جناحي الطائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation takes drawing in the wing as an order to steady and control oneself when the staff becomes a serpent, so Moses will not panic or fear.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن يراد بضم جناحه إليه : تجلده وضبطه نفسه . وتشدده عند انقلاب العصا حية حتى لا يضطرب ولا يرهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The self-control interpretation is a bird metaphor: a frightened bird spreads and slackens its wings, while normally keeping them tucked and raised.
rows.anchor: استعارة من فعل الطائر ؛ لأنه إذا خاف نشر جناحيه وأرخاهما . وإلا فجناحاه مضمومتان إليه مشمران

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: In an anecdote, he comforted an embarrassed scribe who had accidentally passed wind, telling him to take up his pen, draw in his wing, and calm down.
rows.anchor: خذ قلمك ، واضمم إليك جناحك ، وليفرخ روعك ، فإني ما سمعتها من أحد أكثر مما سمعتها من نفسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min al-rahb means because of fear: fear at seeing the serpent is the cause for drawing in the wing.
rows.anchor: ومعنى قوله : ( من الرهب ) من أجل الرهب ، أي : إذا أصابك الرهب عند رؤية الحية فاضمم إليك جناحك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Drawing in the wing and putting the hand into the garment can describe the same action; the different wording serves the distinct goals of showing a white hand and concealing fear.
rows.anchor: معنى : { واضمم إليك جناحك } ، وقوله : { اسلك يدك فى جيبك } على أحد التفسيرين : واحد . ولكن خولف بين العبارتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two commands about drawing the wing together are reconciled by taking the right hand as the wing drawn in and the left hand as the wing it is drawn toward; each hand can be called a wing.
rows.anchor: المراد بالجناح المضموم . هو اليد اليمنى ، وبالمضموم إليه : اليد اليسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the claim that rahb means sleeve in Himyaritic, questioning its reliable attestation, contextual fit, and the claim that Moses wore a sleeveless wool garment.
rows.anchor: ومن بدع التفاسير : أن الرهب : الكم ، بلغة حمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhanak is read lightly as the dual of dhaka or with doubling as the dual of dhalika.
rows.anchor: فذانك } قرىء مخففا ومشددا ، فالمخفف مثنى ذاك . والمشدد مثنى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two proofs are clear and radiant; burhan is named for its brightness, like the term for a very fair woman.
rows.anchor: برهان } حجتان بينتان نيرتان . فإن قلت : لم سميت الحجة برهانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The n in burhan is extra, as shown by abraha for bringing a proof; the term evokes whiteness and illumination.
rows.anchor: لبياضها وإنارتها من قولهم للمرأة البيضاء . برهرهة ، بتكرير العين واللام معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sultan is another name for proof, derived from salit, oil, because proof gives light.
rows.anchor: ونظيره تسميتهم إياها سلطان من السليط وهو الزيت ، لإنارتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If worship and religious life cannot be established in one's present country, the believer should migrate somewhere thought to offer a safer heart, sounder religion, more worship, and better humility.
rows.anchor: فليهاجر عنه إلى بلد يقدر أنه فيه أسلم قلبا وأصح دينا وأكثر عبادة وأحسن خشوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From his experience, the sanctuary and its precincts best help master the ego and desire, gather a distracted heart, ease worry, encourage contentment, repel Satan and many trials, and strengthen religious practice; he thanks God for enabling this.
rows.anchor: فلم نجد فيما درنا وداروا : أعون على قهر النفس وعصيان الشهوة وأجمع للقلب المتلفت

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even by a span, merits Paradise and the companionship of Abraham and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: من فر بدينه من أرض إلى أرض وإن كان شبرا من الأرض ؛ استوجب الجنة وكان رفيق إبراهيم ومحمد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view applies the verse to the oppressed Muslims in Mecca, whose religious practice could not be established among unbelievers, and links it with 4:97.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي في المستضعفين بمكة الذين نزل فيهم : { ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In fa-iyyaya fa-bu'dun, the first-person form contrasts with the third-person and second-person object forms, and is understood as fa-iyyaya fa-bu'du, worship Me.
rows.anchor: فإياى فاعبدون } في المتكلم ، نحو : إياه ضربته ، في الغائب وإياك عضتك ، في المخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa answers an omitted condition: if worship cannot be made sincere in one land, make it sincere elsewhere; fronting the object replaces the deleted condition and conveys exclusivity and sincerity.
rows.anchor: الفاء جواب شرط محذوف ؛ لأن المعنى : إن أرضي واسعة فإن لم تخلصوا العبادة لي في أرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The death verse follows the command to seek a land suited to worship: everyone will experience death's bitterness and anguish, then reach requital, so one must prepare for it with all one's effort.
rows.anchor: كل نفس ذائقة الموت } أي واجدة مرارته وكربه كما يجد الذائق طعم المذوق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report names Luqman's son An'am.
rows.anchor: قيل : كان اسم ابنه ( أنعم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi instead gives Luqman's son's name as Ashkam.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : ( أشكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says Luqman's son and wife were unbelievers, but Luqman kept persuading them until they accepted Islam.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان ابنه وامرأته كافرين ، فما زال بهما حتى أسلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk is an immense injustice because it equates the sole giver of blessings with one who gives none and cannot give any; the enormity is beyond conception.
rows.anchor: لأن التسوية بين من لا نعمة إلا هي منه ، ومن لا نعمة منه البتة ولا يتصور أن تكون منه ظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamalat-hu means his mother carried him while weakened; the phrase is circumstantial and describes weakness increasing as pregnancy grew heavier.
rows.anchor: تهن { وهنا على وهن } كقولك رجع عودا على يده ، بمعنى ؛ يعود عودا على يده ، وهو في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads wahn with both words vowelled, and the source notes the two verb forms wahan-yūhinu and wahan-yahinu.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( وهنا على وهن ) . بالتحريك عن أبي عمرو . يقال : وهن يوهن . ووهن يهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has fasluhu in place of fisaluhu.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( وفصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ashkur is an explanatory gloss for waṣṣaynā: the command is to give thanks.
rows.anchor: أن اشكر } تفسير لوصينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying that one has no knowledge of the supposed partners denies their existence: the idols are nothing, as in 29:42.
rows.anchor: ما ليس لك به علم } أراد بنفي العمل به نفيه ، أي : لا تشرك بي ما ليس بشيء ، يريد الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma'ruf means kind companionship, including good character, forbearance, tolerance, dutiful care, kinship, and what generosity and honor require.
rows.anchor: معروفا } صحابا ، أو مصاحبا معروفا حسنا بخلق جميل وحلم واحتمال وبر وصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the path of those who turn to God means following believers in religion, not one's parents, while still treating the parents well in worldly life.
rows.anchor: واتبع سبيل المؤمنين في دينك ولا تتبع سبيلهما فيه وإن كنت مأمورا بحسن مصاحبتهما في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return to God distinguishes worldly duties toward parents, including honoring and respecting them, from their afterlife judgment: the believer is rewarded for faith and they for disbelief.
rows.anchor: ثم إلي مرجعك ومرجعهما ، فأجازيك على إيمانك وأجازيهما على كفرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage is reported to have been revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and his mother, who went three days without food or drink until her mouth was forced open with a stick.
rows.anchor: وروي : أنها نزلت في سعد بن أبي وقاص وأمه . وفي القصة : أنها مكثت ثلاثا لا تطعم ولا تشرب

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Sa'd said that even if his mother had seventy souls and they all left her, he would not return to disbelief.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه قال : لو كانت لها سبعون نفسا فخرجت ، لما ارتددت إلى الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical instruction about honoring parents interrupts Luqman's counsel as a digression that reinforces his prohibition of shirk.
rows.anchor: هذا الكلام كيف وقع في أثناء وصية لقمان ؟ قلت : هو كلام اعترض به على سبيل الاستطراد ، تأكيدا لما في وصية لقمان من النهي عن الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mother's bearing and weaning are inserted between the command and its gloss to detail her hardship, especially establish the mother's claim to care, and recall her great right.
rows.anchor: لما وصى بالوالدين : ذكر ما تكابده الأم وتعانيه من المشاق والمتاعب في حمله وفصاله هذه المدة المتطاولة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says the warning against hurting Moses was revealed about Zayd and Zaynab and the gossip people circulated about them.
rows.anchor: قيل : نزلت في شأن زيد وزينب ، وما سمع فيه من قالة بعض الناس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account identifies the offense against Moses as a prostitute whom Qarun tried to induce to accuse Moses falsely.
rows.anchor: وقيل : في أذى موسى عليه السلام : هو حديث المومسة التي أرادها قارون على قذفه بنفسها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further account says people accused Moses of killing Aaron; angels carried Aaron's body past them so they would know he had not been murdered.
rows.anchor: وقيل : اتهامهم إياه بقتل هارون ، وكان قد خرج معه الجبل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says God revived Aaron and he testified that Moses was innocent.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أحياه الله فأخبرهم ببراءة موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says people attributed a bodily defect, such as leprosy or a hernia, to Moses, and God showed he was clear of it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : قرفوه بعيب في جسده من برص أو أدرة ، فأطلعهم الله على أنه برىء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wajihan means having rank and standing with God; God therefore removed accusations and harm from Moses as a king protects a favored dignitary.
rows.anchor: وجيها } ذا جاه ومنزلة عنده ، فلذلك كان يميط عنه التهم ، ويدفع الأذى

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود، الأعمش، أبو حيوة
rows.claim: These readers add the words abd Allah in the reading wa-kana abd Allah wajihan; Ibn Khalawayh says he heard Ibn Shanabudh use it in Ramadan prayer.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود والأعمش وأبو حيوة : ( وكان عبد الله وجيها ) قال ابن خالويه : صليت خلف ابن شنبوذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the common reading because it explicitly states Moses' standing with God, like 81:20; the variant does not express that relation.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة أوجه ؛ لأنها مفصحة عن وجاهته عند الله ، كقوله تعالى : { عند ذى العرش مكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mimma qalu means the import of their words—the defamatory matter—rather than speech itself; thus Moses is cleared of the accusation.
rows.anchor: المراد بالقول أو المقول : مؤداه ومضمونه وهو الأمر المعيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He attaches fi hadhihi al-dunya to ahsanu, meaning those who do good in this world receive an indescribably good reward in the afterlife, namely Paradise.
rows.anchor: متعلق بأحسنوا لا بحسنة ، معناه : الذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا فلهم حسنة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi attaches the phrase to hasanah and interprets the worldly good as health and well-being.
rows.anchor: وقد علقه السدي بحسنة ، ففسر بحسنة بالصحة والعافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the phrase cannot be an adjective before hasanah, when it precedes it can specify where the good is located; the order does not prevent the attachment.
rows.anchor: هو صفة لها إذا تأخر فإذا تقدم كان بيانا لمكانها فلم يخل التقدم بالتعلق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the one who calls to God as the Messenger, who called people to Islam.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا إلى الإسلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains doing good as acting rightly with the Lord and making Islam the person’s religious way.
rows.anchor: وعمل صالحا } فيما بينه وبين ربه ، وجعل الإسلام نحلة له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies the people described as the Companions of the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وعنه : أنهم أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says they did not doubt the verse was revealed about the callers to prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها : ما كنا نشك أن هذه الآية نزلت في المؤذنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse applies generally to anyone combining monotheism and commitment to Islam, good works, and calling others to the good; these are learned practitioners among the people of justice and divine unity.
rows.anchor: وهي عامة في كل من جمع بين هذه الثلاث : أن يكون موحدا معتقدا لدين الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying “I am one of the Muslims” expresses Islam as a creed and school, not merely an utterance, as when one names Abu Hanifa’s doctrine his statement.
rows.anchor: ليس الغرض أنه تكلم بهذا الكلام ، ولكن جعل دين الإسلام مذهبه ومعتقده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutila al-kharrasun is a curse wishing death and destruction on them, like 80:17, then functions idiomatically like cursing or vilifying.
rows.anchor: { قتل الخرصون } دعاء عليهم ، كقوله تعالى : { قتل الإنسان ما أكفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharrasun are liars who conjecture false things; the definite article points to the people making contradictory claims.
rows.anchor: والخراصون : الكذابون المقدرون ما لا يصح ، وهم أصحاب القول المختلف ، واللام إشارة إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has kharrasin in the accusative, with God understood as the one who killed them.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( قتل الخراصين ) أي : قتل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fi ghamrah means submerged in ignorance, while sahun means heedless of what they were commanded.
rows.anchor: فى غمرة } في جهل يغمرهم { ساهون } غافلون عما أمروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask in mockery when the Day of Recompense will come.
rows.anchor: فيقولون : ( أيان يوم الدين ) أي متى يوم الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dialect reads ayan with kasrah on the hamzah.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بكسر الهمزة وهي لغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although ayan seems to modify the noun day rather than an event, the intended sense is when the Day of Recompense occurs.
rows.anchor: معناه : أيان وقوع يوم الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day in the answer is governed by an implied verb indicated by the question: the day they are tried in the Fire occurs.
rows.anchor: بفعل مضمر دل عليه السؤال ، أي : يقع يوم هم على النار يفتنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase yawm hum al-nar yuftanun may instead be read with yawm opened because it is annexed to a non-declinable clause.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مفتوحا لإضافته إلى غير متمكن وهي الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the opening, yawm may be accusative under the implied yaqa'u, or nominative as the predicate in huwa yawm.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون محله نصبا بالمضمر الذي هو يقع ؛ ورفعا على هو يوم هم على النار يفتنون

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads yuftanun in the nominative; the passive verb means they are burned and punished.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة بالرفع { يفتنون } يحرقون ويعذبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word fitin means a black-stone desert because its stones look scorched.
rows.anchor: ومنه الفتين : وهي الحرة ؛ لأن حجارتها كأنها محرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhuqu fitnatakum is a circumstantial phrase, with the words spoken to them understood.
rows.anchor: ذوقوا فتنتكم } في محل الحال ، أي : مقولا لهم هذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the subject and alladhi its predicate: this punishment is what you used to demand in haste.
rows.anchor: هذا العذاب هو الذي { كنتم به تستعجلون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, hadha is an appositive of fitnatakum: taste this punishment.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون هذا بدلا من فتنتكم ؛ أي : ذوقوا هذا العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fleeing to God means fleeing to obedience and reward from disobedience and punishment, affirming divine oneness and associating nothing with God.
rows.anchor: ففروا إلى الله } أي إلى طاعته وثوابه من معصيته وعقابه ، ووحدوه ولا تشركوا به شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the warning at the call to obedience and ban on shirk shows faith benefits only with action and action only with faith; salvation requires both.
rows.anchor: ليعلم أن الإيمان لا ينفع إلا مع العمل ، كما أن العمل لا ينفع إلا مع الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is for Muhammad to say, “Flee to God.”
rows.anchor: والمعنى : قل يا محمد : ففروا إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Haqqah is the Hour whose coming is certain and unavoidable, with no doubt.
rows.anchor: الساعة الواجبة الوقوع الثابتة المجيء ، التي هي آتية لا ريب فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that it is the Hour in which the realities of reckoning, reward, and punishment are realized.
rows.anchor: أو التي فيها حواق الأمور من الحساب والثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is that matters become known in their true reality then; haqq means to know something's truth.
rows.anchor: أو التي تحق فيها الأمور ، أي : تعرف على الحقيقة ، من قولك لا أحق هذا ، أي : لا أعرف حقيقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb of becoming real is attributed to the Hour, although in fact the people who experience it are the ones to whom it applies.
rows.anchor: جعل الفعل لها وهو لأهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Haqqah is the subject and ma al-haqqah its predicate; the underlying wording is al-Haqqah ma hiya, with the explicit noun replacing the pronoun for emphasis and awe.
rows.anchor: وارتفاعها على الابتداء وخبرها { ما الحآقة } والأصل : الحاقة ما هي ، أي أي شيء هي تفخيما لشأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma adraka asks what could make one know the Hour's nature; its greatness exceeds anyone's knowledge or imagination, however one imagines it.
rows.anchor: وكيفما قدرت حالها فهي أعظم من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma is nominative, while adraka is suspended from taking an object because it contains an interrogative.
rows.anchor: و ( ما ) في موضع الرفع على الابتداء . و { أدراك } معلق عنه لتضمنه معنى الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qari'ah means the striking calamity: it terrifies people, splits the sky, crushes and scatters mountains and earth, and extinguishes stars.
rows.anchor: القارعة ) التي تقرع الناس بالأفزاع والأهوال ، والسماء بالانشقاق والإنفطار ، والأرض والجبال بالدك والنسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it al-Qari'ah in place of a pronoun evokes the blow itself and further intensifies the description of the Hour's severity.
rows.anchor: وضعت موضع الضمير لتدل على معنى القرع . في الحاقة : زيادة في وصف شدتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After magnifying the Hour, the discourse recounts those who denied it and what befell them, warning the Meccans about the outcome of denial.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكرها وفخمها أتبع ذكر من كذب بها وما حل بهم بسبب التكذيب ، تذكيرا لأهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-taghiyah means an event whose violence exceeds limits.
rows.anchor: بالطاغية } بالواقعة المجاوزة للحد في الشدة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies al-taghiyah as the earthquake.
rows.anchor: واختلف فيها ، فقيل : الرجفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies al-taghiyah as the thunderbolt.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : الصاعقة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God sent a cry that silenced and killed them.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : بعث الله عليهم صيحة فأهمدتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal that al-taghiyah is a verbal noun meaning their transgression is unlikely because it does not pair well with the following fierce wind.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الطاغية مصدر كالعافية ، أي : بطغيانهم ؛ وليس بذاك لعدم الطباق بينها وبين قوله { بريح صرصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sarsar can mean a fiercely loud wind that makes a sharp repeated sound.
rows.anchor: والصرصر : الشديدة الصوت لها صرصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively sarsar means bitterly cold, from sarr; its repeated cold is so intense that it burns.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الباردة من الصر ، كأنها التي كرر فيها البرد وكثر : فهي تحرق لشدة بردها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Atiyah describes a fiercely violent wind, using rebellion metaphorically; it also means the wind exceeded control and tore people from every refuge.
rows.anchor: عاتية } شديدة العصف والعتو استعارة . أو عتت على عاد ، فما قدروا على ردها بحيلة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the wind rebelled against its keepers and escaped their control.
rows.anchor: وقيل : عتت على خزانها ، فخرجت بلا كيل ولا وزن

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says God sends each wind and drop of rain in measured amounts, except in Noah's and Aad's times: floodwaters overwhelmed their keepers, and Aad's wind escaped them; it cites 69:11 and 69:6.
rows.anchor: ما أرسل الله سفينة من ريح إلا بمكيال ولا قطرة من مطر إلا بمكيال إلا يوم عاد ويوم نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's language may simply express exceptional intensity and excess.
rows.anchor: ولعلها عبارة عن الشدة والإفراط فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Husuman may be a plural of hasim or a verbal noun, analogous to shukur and kufur.
rows.anchor: الحسوم : لا يخلو من أن يكون جمع حاسم كشهود وقعود . أو مصدرا كالشكور والكفور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a plural, it means ill-omened days that cut off every good and blessing.
rows.anchor: فمعنى قوله : { حسوما } نحسات حسمت كل خير واستأصلت كل بركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a plural, it can mean winds blowing in uninterrupted succession until they destroyed the people, like repeated cauterization to excise a disease.
rows.anchor: أو متتابعة هبوب الرياح : ماخفتت ساعة حتى أتت عليهم تمثيلا لتتابعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a verbal noun, husuman may govern an omitted verb meaning to eradicate completely, describe the wind as having that quality, or state its purpose as annihilation.
rows.anchor: فإما أن ينتصب بفعله مضمرا ، أي : تحسم حسوما ، بمعنى تستأصل استئصالا . أو يكون صفة كقولك : ذات حسوم

rows.speaker: عبد العزيز بن زرارة الكلابي
rows.claim: His line's phrase years of husum illustrates successive years.
rows.anchor:
وقال عبد العزيز ابن زرارة الكلابي :
ففرق بين بينهم زمان … تتابع فيه أعوام حسوم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reads husuman with fathah as a circumstantial accusative describing the wind as annihilating.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السدى ( حسوما ) ، بالفتح حالا من الريح ، أي : سخرها عليهم مستأصلة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say these were the Days of the Old Woman: an elderly woman of Aad hid in a tunnel, but the wind pulled her out and killed her on day eight.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي أيام العجوز ؛ وذلك أن عجوزا من عاد توارت في سرب ، فانتزعتها الريح في اليوم الثامن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the days with winter's end and lists their traditional names, including al-sinn, al-sanbar, al-wabr, al-amir, al-mu'tamir, al-mu'allil and extinguishing the embers.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي أيام العجز ، وهي آخر الشتاء : وأسماؤها : الصن والصنبر ، والوبر . والآمر ، والمؤتمر ، والمعلل ، ومطفىء الجمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sakhkharaha alayhim means He subjected the wind to them as He willed.
rows.anchor: معنى { سخرها عليهم } سلطها عليهم كما شا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fiha may refer to the wind's paths or to the nights and days.
rows.anchor: في مهابها . أو في الليالي والأيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has a'jaz nakhil with the plural of the palm trunk.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( أعجاز نخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min baqiyah may mean a remnant, any surviving person, or a trace of survival, as al-taghiyah can mean transgression.
rows.anchor: من باقية } من بقية أو من نفس باقية . أو من بقاء ، كالطاغية : بمعنى الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an interrogative, hal means qad; its original form was a-hal, as the cited line shows, so the verse asks whether a time has indeed passed, with emphasis and approximation.
rows.anchor:
هل بمعنى ( قد ) في الاستفهام خاصة ، والأصل : أهل ، بدليل قوله :
أهل رأونا بسفع القاع ذي الأكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time passed over humanity shortly before now, when the human being was not mentioned, existing only as a sperm in the loins.
rows.anchor: أتى على الإنسان قبل زمان قريب { حين من الدهر لم يكن } فيه { شيئا مذكورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insan here means the human species, as verse 2 says humanity was created from a drop.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالإنسان : جنس بني آدم ، بدليل قوله : { إنا خلقنا الإنسان من نطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the unmentioned time can be parsed as a circumstantial clause modifying insan, or as an adjective describing hin.
rows.anchor: محله النصب على الحال من الإنسان ، كأنه قيل : هل أتى عليه حين من الدهر غير مذكور . أو الرفع على الوصف لحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone who heard the verse wished that the state of being uncreated and unaccountable had lasted to completion.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم : أنها تليت عنده فقال : ليتها تمت ، أراد : ليت تلك الحالة تمت ، وهي كونه شيئا غير مذكور ولم يخلق ولم يكلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amshaj and mashaj are singular forms, like other lexical singulars, and can describe singular nutfah; amshaj is not a broken plural.
rows.anchor: نطفة أمشاج } كبرمة أعشار ، وبرد أكياش : وهي ألفاظ مفردة غير جموع ، ولذلك وقعت صفات للأفراد

rows.speaker: الشماخ
rows.claim: Al-Shammakh's verse uses mashaj for the mixed substance, illustrating the singular form.
rows.anchor:
قال الشماخ :
طوت أحشاء مرتجة لوقت … على مشج سلالته مهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mashaj and mazaj mean mixed; the drop consists of two fluids mingled together.
rows.anchor: ومشجه ومزجه : بمعنى . والمعنى من نطفة قد امتزج لها الما آن

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says amshaj refers to the veins in the semen.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود : هي عروق النطفة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says amshaj means varied colors and stages: first a drop, then a clot, then a morsel.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : أمشاج ألوان وأطوار ، يريد : أنها تكون نطفة ، ثم علقة ، ثم مضغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabtali-hi is circumstantial: God created him intending to test him; alternatively it names his transfer from one state to another metaphorically as a trial.
rows.anchor: نبتليه } في موضع الحال ، أي : خلقناه مبتلين له ، بمعنى : مريدين ابتلاءه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the testing as God's moving the fetus through stages in the womb, from a drop to a clot.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : نصرفه في بطن أمه نطفة ثم علقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal that nabtali-hi is temporally delayed, meaning God gave hearing and sight in order to test the person, is forced.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو في تقدير التأخير ، يعني : فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا لنبتليه ، وهو من التعسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tatfif is cheating in measure or weight by shorting someone a slight, trifling amount.
rows.anchor: التطفيف : البخس في الكيل والوزن : لأن ما يبخس شيء طفيف حقير

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the people of Medina were the worst measurers when the Prophet arrived; the warning came down and they improved their measuring.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قدم المدينة وكانوا من أخبث الناس كيلا ، فنزلت فأحسنوا الكيل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says a Medinan called Abu Juhaynah had two measures, using one when selling and another when buying.
rows.anchor: وقيل : قدمها وبها رجل يعرف بأبي جهينة ومعه صاعان : بكيل بأحدهما ويكتال بالآخر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A further report says Medinan merchants cheated in trade through munabadha, mulamasa, and mukhatara; the surah came down and the Prophet recited it to them.
rows.anchor: كان أهل المدينة تجارا يطففون ، وكانت بياعاتهم المنابذة والملامسة والمخاطرة ، فنزلت فخرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقرأها عليهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says five social violations bring five calamities: breaking covenants brings enemy domination; judging without revelation spreads poverty; public indecency spreads death; cheating measures withholds crops and brings drought; withholding zakat blocks rain.
rows.anchor: ما نقض قوم العهد إلا سلط الله عليهم عدوهم ، وما حكموا بغير ما أنزل الله إلا فشا فيهم الفقر

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali told a man who was weighing saffron with an excess to establish the fair weight first, then add whatever he wished, habituating fairness and distinguishing duty from extra giving.
rows.anchor: مر برجل يزن الزعفران وقد أرجح فقال له : أقم الوزن بالقسط ، ثم أرجح بعد ذلك ما شئت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas warns Persians that they were entrusted with measures and scales, by which earlier peoples perished; he singles them out because they use both, unlike Mecca's weighing and Medina's measuring.
rows.anchor: إنكم معشر الأعاجم وليتم أمرين : بهما هلك من كان قبلكم : المكيال والميزان ؛ وخص الأعاجم

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar warned sellers to fear God and fulfill measures, saying cheats will be halted before the Majestic Lord until sweat reaches their mouths.
rows.anchor: اتق الله وأوف الكيل ، فإن المطففين يوقفون يوم القيامة لعظمة الرحمن حتى إن العرق ليلجمهم

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima testified that every measurer or weigher is in Hell; when told his own son did that work, he repeated the testimony about his son.
rows.anchor: أشهد أن كل كيال ووزان في النار . فقيل له : إن ابنك كيال أو وزان ؛ فقال : أشهد أنه في النار

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy says not to seek one's needs from people who earn their living at the tops of measures and tongues of scales.
rows.anchor: لا تلتمس الحوائج ممن رزقه في رؤوس المكاييل وألسن الموازين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using ala where min might be expected signals that their taking from people harms and oppresses them.
rows.anchor: لما كان اكتيالهم من الناس اكتيالا يضرهم ويتحامل فيه عليهم : أبدل ( على ) مكان ( من ) للدلالة على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ala attaches to yastawfun, with the object fronted to stress that they take full measure from others in particular while taking their own in full.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يتعلق ( على ) بيستوفون ، ويقدم المفعول على الفعل لإفادة الخصوصية ، أي : يستوفون على الناس خاصة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says min and ala alternate here: iktaltu alayka means I took what was due from you, while iktaltu minka means I received it from you.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء ( من ) و ( على ) يعتقبان في هذا الموضع ، لأنه حق عليه ؛ فإذا قال اكتلت عليك ، فكأنه قال : أخذت ما عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In kaluhum and wazanuhum, the pronoun refers to people as direct objects, with the preposition removed and the verb made transitive; cited poetry likewise uses the verb for someone.
rows.anchor: وفيه وجهان : أن يراد كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم ؛ فحذف الجار وأوصل الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun stands for the omitted measured or weighed amount, with the genitive noun taking its place.
rows.anchor: وأن يكون على حذف المضاف وإقامة المضاف إليه مقامه ، والمضاف هو المكيل أو الموزون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects making the pronoun the subject referring to the cheaters: that reverses the point from how they treat recipients to who performs the act, producing incoherent discourse.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح أن يكون ضميرا مرفوعا للمطففين ، لأن الكلام يخرج به إلى نظم فاسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also rejects relying on the mushaf's omission of the alif after plural waw to rule out the subject reading; orthography is not consistently conventional and the alif is not pronounced or meaningful.
rows.anchor: والتعلق في إيطاله بخط المصحف ، وأن الألف التي تكتب بعد واو الجمع غير ثابتة فيه : ركيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif after plural waw merely distinguishes it visually from a singular verb, and some scribes omit it because context already distinguishes the forms.
rows.anchor: وإنما كتبت هذه الألف تفرقة بين واو الجمع وغيرها في نحو قولك : هم لم يدعوا

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر، حمزة
rows.claim: Isa ibn Umar and Hamza do read the pronouns as referring to the cheaters, pausing at both waw letters to make their reading clear.
rows.anchor: وعن عيسى بن عمر وحمزة : أنهما كانا يرتكبان ذلك ، أي يجعلان الضميرين للمطففين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They likely buy only by measure, since it lets them steal by manipulating how full the measure is; when giving, either measure or weight lets them shortchange.
rows.anchor: كأن المطففين كانوا لا يأخذون ما يكال ويوزن إلا بالمكاييل دون الموازين لتمكنهم بالاكتيال من الاستيفاء والسرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yukhsirun means they diminish the amount; one says a scale loses or causes a loss.
rows.anchor: يخسرون } ينقصون يقال : خسر الميزان وأخسره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A-la yadhunnu is a powerful rebuke and expression of astonishment that they never even imagine being resurrected and held to account for the smallest amount.
rows.anchor: ألا يظن } إنكار وتعجيب عظيم من حالهم في الاجتراء على التطفيف

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada exhorts: give people their full due as you want yours fulfilled, and be fair as you want fairness shown to you.
rows.anchor: أوف يا ابن آدم كما تحب أن يوفى لك ، وأعدل كما تحب أن يعدل لك

rows.speaker: الفضيل
rows.claim: Al-Fudayl says shortchanging the scale blackens one's face on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وعن الفضيل : بخس الميزان سواد الوجه يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: عبد الملك بن مروان
rows.claim: A Bedouin rebuked Abd al-Malik: if cheaters face this threat, what of a ruler taking Muslims' property without measuring it?
rows.anchor: فما ظنك بنفسك وأنت تأخذ أموال المسلمين بلا كيل ولا وزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke, word choice, mighty Day, humbled people, and title Lord of the Worlds expose the enormity of short measure and every related injustice: unfairness in transactions and failure of equity in all words and acts.
rows.anchor: بيان بليغ لعظم الذنب وتفاقم الإثم في التطفيف وفيما كان في مثل حاله من الحيف وترك القيام بالقسط

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes yadhunnu to mean certainty; al-Zamakhshari prefers the interpretation he gave earlier.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الظن بمعنى اليقين ، والوجه ما ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm yaqumu is accusative under mab'uthun.
rows.anchor: ونصب { يوم يقوم } بمبعوثون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has yawm in the genitive as an appositive to yawmin azim.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالجر بدلا من ( يوم عظيم

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar wept so intensely when reciting the verse about people standing before the Lord that he could not continue.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عمر أنه قرأ هذه السورة فلما بلغ قوله : { يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين } بكى نحيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamz means breaking, as in hazm, and lamz means stabbing; both describe breaking people's reputations, belittling them, backbiting, and attacking them.
rows.anchor: الهمز : الكسر ، كالهزم . واللمز : الطعن . يقال : لمزه ولهزه طعنه ، والمراد : الكسر من أعراض الناس والغض منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pattern fa'lah indicates a habitual trait that has become ingrained, as with la'nah and dahikah.
rows.anchor: وبناء ( فعلة ) يدل على أن ذلك عادة منه قد ضرى بها . ونحوهما : اللعنة والضحكة

rows.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
rows.claim: An unattributed verse uses hamiz and lamiz as names for the habitual slanderer.
rows.anchor:
قال :
وإن أغيب فأنت الهامز اللمزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has al-hamzah al-lamzah, without the extra kull.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ويل للهمزة اللمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading leaves the m of lamzah unvowelled; it denotes a clown who tells bizarre jokes, is laughed at, and is insulted.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ويل لكل همزة لمزة ) بسكون الميم : وهو المسخرة الذي يأتي بالأوابد والأضاحيك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One occasion report says the surah was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, who habitually backbit and disparaged people.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق وكانت عادته الغيبة والوقيعة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says it was revealed about Umayya ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: وقيل : في أمية بن خلف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says it concerned al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who backbit and disparaged the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وقيل : في الوليد بن المغيرة واغتيابه لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وغضه منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the occasion was specific, the warning is general to everyone who commits this offense, and indirect address to the original target is especially deterrent.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون السبب خاصا والوعيد عاما ، ليتناول كل من باشر ذلك القبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase alladhi may be an appositive to kull or an accusative of censure.
rows.anchor: الذى } بدل من كل . أو نصب على الذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading intensifies the verb jama'a, matching the repeated count in the expression.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( جمع ) بالتشديد ، وهو مطابق لعدده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of addadahu is that he made wealth a provision against the contingencies of time.
rows.anchor: وقيل : { * عدده } جعله عدة لحوادث الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with wa means he collected wealth and counted or enumerated it.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( وعدده ) أي : جمع المال وضبط عدده وأحصاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that he amassed wealth and people who support him; a person of addad has many helpers and resources.
rows.anchor: أو جمع ماله وقومه الذين ينصرونه ، من قولك : فلان ذو عدد وعدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, malan wa-addadahu means he amassed wealth and counted it, with the form simplified as in the cited word.
rows.anchor: وقيل : { مالا وعدده } معناه : وعده على فك الإدغام ، نحو : ضننوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhledahu and khalladahu both mean that wealth lengthened his hopes until he imagined it would keep him alive forever.
rows.anchor: أخلده } وخلده بمعنى أي : طول المال أمله ، ومناه الأماني البعيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he builds fortified homes, plants trees, and develops the land as though wealth made him live forever.
rows.anchor: أو يعمل من تشييد البنيان الموثق بالصخر والآجر وغرس الأشجار وعمارة الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation makes the wording an ironic allusion to good works, which truly make their doer abide in bliss; wealth does not.
rows.anchor: أو هو تعريض بالعمل الصالح . وأنه هو الذي أخلد صاحبه في النعيم ؛ فأما المال فما أخلد أحدا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say al-Akhnas had either four thousand or ten thousand dinars.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه كان للأخنس أربعة آلاف دينار . وقيل : عشرة آلاف

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan challenged a wealthy visitor about thousands he neither used to ransom a base person nor gave to a generous one; the man saved it against hardship, and Hasan said he would leave it to an ungrateful heir and return it to an unforgiving Lord.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : أنه عاد موسرا فقال : ما تقول في ألوف لم أفتد بها من لئيم ولا تفضلت على كريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes the man's belief that wealth made him immortal.
rows.anchor: كلا } ردع له عن حسبانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has the dual verb, so both the man and his wealth are cast away.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( لينبذان ) أي : هو وماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading has a dammah on dhal, taking the man and his supporters as the ones cast away; a further reading has a singular object suffix.
rows.anchor: ولينبذن ، بضم الذال ، أي : هو وأنصاره . ولينبذنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hutamah is a fire that crushes whatever is thrown into it; a voracious eater can also be called hutamah.
rows.anchor: فى الحطمة } في النار التي من شأنها أن تحطم كل ما يلقى فيها . ويقال للرجل الأكول : إنه لحطمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has al-hatimah; the fire enters their bodies, reaches the chests and hearts, the body's most delicate and pain-sensitive core, and overwhelms them.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( الحاطمة ) يعني أنها تدخل في أجوافهم حتى تصل إلى صدورهم وتطلع على أفئدتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hearts may be singled out as the places of disbelief, false beliefs, and corrupt intentions; the fire's looking upon them means it rises over, dominates, and envelops them.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يخص الأفئدة لأنها مواطن الكفر والعقائد الفاسدة والنيات الخبيثة . ومعنى اطلاع النار عليها : أنها تعلوها وتغلبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mu'sadah means tightly closed and sealed.
rows.anchor: تحن إلى أجبال مكة ناقتي

rows.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
rows.claim: An unattributed poem describing Sana'a's closed gates illustrates the meaning of mu'sadah.
rows.anchor: تحن إلى أجبال مكة ناقتي … ومن دونها أبواب صنعاء موصده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fi amad has readings with two damma vowels, with a silent middle consonant, or with two fathas.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( في عمد ) بضمتين . وعمد ، بسكون الميم . وعمد بفتحتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first interpretation stresses their hopelessness of escape and certainty of endless confinement: doors are shut and bars stretched over them, reinforcing the closure.
rows.anchor: يؤكد يأسهم من الخروج وتيقنهم يحبس الأبد ، فتؤصد عليهم الأبواب وتمدد على الأبواب العمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they are shut in while restrained in long stocks or pillories like those used to confine thieves.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى : أنها عليهم مؤصدة ، موثقين في عمد ممددة مثل المقاطر التي تقطر فيها اللصوص

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says reciting Surat al-Humazah earns ten good deeds for every person who mocked Muhammad and his Companions.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة الهمزة أعطاه الله عشر حسنات بعدد من استهزأ بمحمد وأصحابه
